  description. Nothing else.
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ☐ Grouping

When displaying the list of sessions in the sidebar rail, should they be
grouped by the filesystem folder they were launched from, or by the git
repository they belong to, so that related work stays visually clustered
together?

  1. By folder
     Sessions are grouped under the exact working directory they were
     started in. This keeps worktrees and subdirectories separate even
     when they share a repo. It's the most literal mapping, but can
     fragment one project into many groups.
  2. By repository
     Sessions are grouped by the git repository root, regardless of which
     subfolder they launched from. Worktrees and subdirectory sessions
     collapse into one project group. Non-repo sessions would need a
     fallback bucket, likely their folder.
  3. Hybrid
     Group by repository when one is detected, and fall back to folder
     grouping otherwise. This gives clean project clustering without
     orphaning non-repo sessions. It's slightly more logic, but probably
     matches user intuition best.
❯ 4. neither — group by whatever the tmux session says
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
